dimensions.assessment: Affects park visitors, park management, and the specific wild horse population in one park unit.
dimensions.evidence: maintain a genetically diverse herd of horses in the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park... with a population of not fewer than 150 horses

dimensions.assessment: Changes management requirements for a single park herd, ensuring protection and monitoring.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall not remove, or assist in or permit the removal of, any horses from Federal land... unless the removal is carried out as part of a plan

dimensions.assessment: Requires developing a cost-effective management plan and conducting annual monitoring and assessments, with no stated funding amount.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall annually monitor, assess, and make available to the public findings

dimensions.assessment: Amends administrative rules for a specific national park unit regarding wildlife management.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5 of the Act of April 25, 1947... is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent management mandates for the park.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall maintain a genetically diverse herd of horses in the South Unit

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for the management plan and annual monitoring
importance_detail.rationale: This bill mandates that the Department of the Interior maintain a minimum population of 150 wild horses in the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park, restricts removals, and requires ongoing monitoring and a management plan.
